note: Maps Windows event providers/messages to plain English. First match wins (order matters).

themes.title: DCOM / COM timeouts
themes.plainEnglish: Background Windows components talking to each other slowly. Extremely common clutter — almost never a problem by itself.

themes.title: Brother printer software chatter
themes.plainEnglish: Printer software complaining it has no IP or a feature is offline. Only matters if printing or scanning actually breaks.

themes.title: Disk retries / storage hiccups
themes.plainEnglish: Windows had to retry reading or writing a drive. Often a USB/portable SSD glitch or a dying disk. Worth watching.

themes.title: GPU driver recovered from a stall
themes.plainEnglish: The graphics driver recovered (nvlddmkm / display timeout). Not always a full crash — care if you saw black screens or freezes.

themes.title: Ethernet link up/down
themes.plainEnglish: The wired network cable link went down and came back (or the adapter reset). Care if the internet actually drops.

themes.title: Unexpected reboot / power loss (Event 41)
themes.plainEnglish: Windows shut down without a clean goodbye — power cut, freeze, or hard reset. Match this to outages or forced reboots you remember.

themes.title: ACPI / embedded controller chatter
themes.plainEnglish: Board firmware talking to the EC chip. Common on ASUS and gaming boards. Usually harmless noise.

themes.title: USB device errors
themes.plainEnglish: A USB device failed to start, reset, or was removed unexpectedly. Check dongles, hubs, and power settings.

themes.title: Windows Update noise
themes.plainEnglish: Update agent messages. Most are routine; only care if updates keep failing.

themes.title: Service start/stop messages
themes.plainEnglish: A Windows service started, stopped, or failed. One-offs are normal; repeated failures need a look.
themes.care: If a feature you use is broken

themes.title: TLS / Schannel certificate noise
themes.plainEnglish: Secure-connection certificate warnings from Windows. Often apps with odd TLS setups — not usually your whole PC.
themes.care: If a specific app cannot connect securely

themes.title: Filter Manager / antivirus stack
themes.plainEnglish: File-system filter messages (often AV or backup). Frequent after security product changes.
themes.care: If files fail to open after installing AV

defaultTheme.title: Other system/application messages
defaultTheme.plainEnglish: Windows logged errors or warnings that do not match a known theme yet. Expand for raw provider names.
defaultTheme.care: Skim if something actually feels broken
